Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Power Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Power Holdings' Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Vargas, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; Elena Torres, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Amanda Lee, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational execution across our 25-gigawatt diversified generation fleet spanning thermal, nuclear, renewables, and storage assets in key U.S. markets like the Southeast, ERCOT, PJM, and the Midwest. Before diving deeper, let me share our perspective on the key industry trends and challenges shaping this landscape, as they frame our outperformance.

Electrification is the dominant megatrend, with U.S. electricity demand expected to grow 4-5% annually through the decade per EIA forecasts, a sharp reversal from the flat 2010s. Data centers from hyperscalers like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud have committed to over 100 gigawatts of new load, equivalent to another California on the grid. In our territories, ERCOT peaks are up 15% year-over-year from AI and crypto, while EVs could add 200-300 terawatt-hours annually by 2030 per IEA estimates.

Decarbonization accelerates this: solar LCOE under $25 per megawatt-hour unsubsidized, wind at $25-50 per Lazard, with 510 gigawatts added globally in 2023. The IRA's 30-50% ITCs have spurred $100 billion in capital, battery storage at 14 gigawatts last year with 85-90% efficiency at $150 per kilowatt-hour. Our 8-gigawatt renewables pipeline, including 3 gigawatts solar-plus-storage under PPAs, benefits with 32% wind and 28% solar capacity factors via bifacial panels and trackers.

Challenges persist: 2.5-terawatt interconnection queues with 5-7 year waits per FERC, transformer lead times at 48-60 months up 300% in price. Gas volatility—Henry Hub spiked 150% to $4.50 last Q4—hits our 4-gigawatt CCGTs, coal retirements risk reliability, weather like Idalia costs billions. Regulatory flux, ROE compression from 5.2% debt costs, cybersecurity up 30%, talent wars for engineers.

Regionally, Southeast stabilizes via coal-to-gas and solar, ERCOT flexes at 35% renewables capacity factor but with price swings, Europe pays 3x for gas, Asia mandates cleaner tech. We're acting: 60% of $4.5 billion 2024-2028 capex to clean energy, 2 gigawatts BESS, nuclear at 93%, SMR pilots, CCUS for 45Q credits. Supply chain locked with 5-year offtakes, talent via PowerTech Academy. This sets 8-10% EPS growth, 9% ROIC, 3.5x debt/EBITDA, 60% FCF returns.

Now, more on our drivers: strong operational performance via O&M efficiencies; renewables portfolio growth; cost management; infrastructure investments; successful GreenWave Renewables integration; Clean Horizon sustainability; positive Georgia PSC outcomes; enhanced Southeast community engagement. Michael will expand on several key financial and operational aspects shortly.

I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss the financials.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.38, surpassing guidance midpoint of $1.32 and consensus by $0.06—our eighth straight beat. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.42, up 12% from $1.27 last year. Year-to-date adjusted EPS is $4.12, up 15%, on track for full-year $5.60-$5.80, lifted by thermal dispatch and transmission ROEs.

Revenue rose 8% to $2.85 billion on 6% regulated volumes, normalized weather, higher PJM/ERCOT wholesale. Retail up 4.2% on 15% above-normal cooling degrees, data centers adding 1.2 gigawatts PPAs and $150 million CWIP revenue. Fleet availability 93.5% via AI predictive maintenance cutting outages 22%, deferring $45 million O&M. Gas CCGTs captured $28 per megawatt-hour spark spreads, renewables output up 28% to 1.8 million megawatt-hours. Gross margins expanded 220 basis points to 42.5%, fuel down 11% on $2.75 Henry Hub hedges, O&M flat at $420 million. Operating EPS up 14%, offset by interest; tax at 21.5% with $60 million PTC/ITCs; buybacks added $0.07. This validates our Reliable Renewables framework, with grid modernization poised for $0.15 2025 EPS upside. Q4 guide $1.55-$1.65.

Turning to O&M expense management and efficiency gains, a key value driver amid inflation on labor, supplies, EPA MATS revisions, gas volatility. Q3 consolidated O&M at $285 million, down 7.2% or $22 million year-over-year; trailing twelve months 18.4% of revenues versus 21.1% last year—better than Duke's 19.8%, matching NextEra's 18.2%. From our 2023 Operational Resilience program, targeting $150 million annualized savings by 2025, we're at 105% trajectory with $68 million banked trailing twelve months.

Digital transformation leads: AI predictive maintenance on 85% of 25-gigawatt fleet using GE Vernova Predix and 50,000 IoT sensors slashed forced outages 22% to 3.2%, availability to 92.4%. At 1,200-megawatt Riverton coal-to-gas plant, avoided $14 million downtime; CCGT heat rates improved 1.8%, saving $8.5 million fuel. Workforce optimized—OSHA rate 0.42—via Siemens MindSphere, RPA, drone inspections for 12% productivity, $11 million labor savings, 5% headcount cut in Southeast.

Regionally, Southeast 9.1% decline via SCR retrofits saving $4.2 million reagents; Southwest renewables 11% per-megawatt drop with Enphase IQ8, 25% fewer panels; Midwest gas 5% softer on $1.20 Appalachia premium, but 80% hedged at $2.75. Savings fund hydrogen pilots targeting 10% heat rate gains by 2026; exited coal logistics saving $9 million yearly. Non-fuel escalation 2.1% versus 4.3% PPI. Q4 $18-20 million more savings, full-year flat to down 6%, $0.12 EPS accretion, $75 million free cash flow for dividends, $2.5 billion capex.

Rate base stood at $28.4 billion end-Q3, up 6.1% year-over-year, strongest in 5.8% CAGR, full-year ~6.3%; organic 7.2% excluding equity issuance. $2.7 billion capex, 65% in-service earning 8.2% AFUDC. Transmission up 8.4% on $850 million 345 kV lines, FERC/MISO-approved, now 22% of base. Distribution 5.9% on $1.1 billion undergrounding, AMI to 85% of 4.2 million customers. Generation 4.2% from 300-megawatt SunForge Solar adding $450 million at 10.1% ROE.

Drivers: modernization for weather like SPP vortex, 95% recovery in Georgia PSC for $600 million hardening, microgrids; decarbonization via IRA, $400 million ERCOT wind-BESS, CCUS on Indiana coal for $1.5 billion potential, nuclear uprates; load growth 4-6% from data centers, 1.2 gigawatts Virginia wheeling, EV substations, 50,000-home VPPs. Headwinds: AFUDC down 50 bps, supply delays, regulatory lag on 10.3% ROE, 9% depreciation rise offset by 3.2% asset life extensions. Guide 6-7% CAGR to 2028 on $15 billion capex—45% T&D, 30% renewables/storage, 15% nuclear/modern, 10% customer.

On dividend policy and payout strategy, board declared $0.65 quarterly, $2.60 annualized, up 4%, yielding 4.2%—above NextEra's 3.1%, Duke's 4.0%. 28-year streak, 60-70% adjusted net income target; Q3 64% versus 68% last year on 12% ANI to $1.45/share from ERCOT $55 per megawatt-hour gas, PJM 9.75% ROE. FFO 2.1x coverage above 1.8x minimum, FCF 58% ratio, 92% conversion post-maintenance capex.

Balances returns with $4.8 billion 2025 capex: 65% growth like 1.5 gigawatts BESS, $800 million offshore wind, $500 million SMR. Northeast regulated bedrock, ERCOT upside, Australia JV tax advantages. 2025 payout low-60s on 8-10% EPS to $5.90-$6.10 from renewables, transmission. ATM $1.5 billion, $3.2 billion liquidity support defensive 4% yield +5% growth.

Investments in renewables and clean transition: Q3 $1.2 billion capex, YTD $4.8 billion up 35%, 62% budget; 24-month $12 billion for 3.2 gigawatts, renewables 48% mix at 35% capacity factor. Solar 1.8 gigawatts including 650-megawatt Desert Bloom with First Solar bifacials, Nextracker, $25 per megawatt-hour LCOE, $32 per megawatt-hour PPAs. Wind: 450-megawatt Prairie Winds III Siemens Gamesa at 42%, 50% 800-megawatt Atlantic Horizon offshore. BESS 1.2 gigawatt-hours like 300-megawatt/1,200-megawatt-hour Vertex Peak Shaver Tesla Megapacks, $15 million frequency revenue, Form Energy pilots.

60/30/10 ERCOT/PJM/CAISO; Iberdrola Spain JV, Australia 500-megawatt. 14.5% Q3 ROIC, 85% hedged, $120 million RECs/LCFS, Scope 1 down 28%, MSCI AAA, $2 billion green bonds. Raise 2024-2026 capex $18-20 billion for 8 gigawatts, 15% FFO CAGR; hedge EPC risks.

Grid modernization/smart grid: $2.8 billion since 2021, 18% CAGR, $450 million opex savings, SAIDI down 32%. AMI 4.7 million Landis+Gyr Revelo/Oracle, 12% peak shave, $28 million TOU revenue, edge AI for losses. ADMS GE 4.0 on 85% substations, FLISR <60 seconds, SAIFI 0.85; DERMS Siemens for 1.2 gigawatts VPPs, $10 million LCAP. Zero-trust $180 million Dragos, 99.99% availability. 2,500 miles dynamic ratings +25% capacity, microgrids 98.5% Idalia uptime, $50 million IIJA. EV V2G 150 megawatts $5 million ancillaries, HEMs 10-15% savings.

$1.2 billion annual to 2028, 12% IRR, 7% rate base growth. FERC 2222 $75 million DER, supply stockpiles, linemen certified. 20% EBITDA growth by 2026 in $100 billion T&D market.

Progress on strategic initiatives/long-term goals: clean transition added 1,200 megawatts YTD to 8.5 gigawatts/42% mix; 450-megawatt SunForge 28% factor, 800-megawatt PPAs $1.2 billion revenue. Wind repower 350 megawatts +25% output; 5-gigawatt pipeline 85% permitted. Grid: 1.2 gigawatt-hours BESS IronPeak 65% utilization $150 million ancillaries, NexusGrid losses -12%, VPP 200 megawatts. CCGTs 95% availability, 20% hydrogen; nuclear life extensions $300 million rate base. Closed $1.8 billion GreenWave 900 megawatts, Orsted JV offshore 2 gigawatts Vestas. Renewables margins 85%, 12% ROE. 50-gigawatt/70% carbon-free by 2035, 6-8% AFFO, 5% yield trajectory; $4 billion liquidity.

Our capex Q3 was $1.2 billion, focused on renewables and grid modernization. Balance sheet strong, committed to shareholders. Anticipate 8-10% EPS growth through 2026.

Lisa Vargas: Thank you, Michael. On operations, improved efficiency in our CCGT plants from AI-driven predictive maintenance resulted in 22% outage reduction and 22% output increase. Outage rates down across the fleet.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Strategically, exploring BESS opportunities, key growth driver. Evaluating acquisitions in ERCOT.

Elena Torres: Thank you, David. Technology investments in grid modernization, cybersecurity via zero-trust Dragos platform. Piloting ADMS in Northeast feeders.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Elena. Regulatory approval for transmission rate case at FERC, allowing $600 million recovery at 10.25% ROE.

Amanda Lee: Thank you, Robert. Community outreach in Southeast boosted positive sentiment 25%.

Johnathan Reyes: Thank you, Michael, Lisa, David, Elena, Robert, and Amanda. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Chris Taylor with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Chris Taylor: Good morning. Can you elaborate on plans for renewable investments?

Johnathan Reyes: Certainly. As Michael detailed, we're accelerating with $18-20 billion capex for 8 gigawatts more, hybrids with BESS, offshore pilots, strong PPAs—positioned for data center demand.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: What is your outlook for EPS?

Michael Chen: Solid 8-10% growth through 2026 from rate base expansion, renewables ROIC, O&M savings, grid revenues—Q4 $1.55-$1.65 on track for $5.60-$5.80 full-year.

Operator: Our next question comes from Ben Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Kim: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain and grid constraints?

Lisa Vargas: Through hedging, domestic sourcing like CATL Georgia, stockpiles for transformers, and dynamic ratings boosting capacity 20-25%—our queue reforms prioritize ready projects.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel: What is the anticipated impact of regulatory changes on earnings?

Robert Kline: Constructive—Georgia PSC, FERC approvals secure ROEs, IRA credits add $15 per megawatt-hour; monitoring state RPS but diversified footprint de-risks.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Reyes for closing remarks.

Johnathan Reyes: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and commitment to long-term shareholder value. Focused on priorities, positioning Nexus Power Holdings for success. Thank you for your time and interest.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
